A 32-year-old man arrives at the emergency department following a motor vehicle collision in which he
was the unrestrained driver and sustained significant trauma to his left arm, which was outside the car
window during the crash. The patient reports pain in his elbow and arm. He has no prior medical history
and is not on any medications. Vital signs are as follows: temperature 99.0°F (37.1°C), blood pressure
106/74 mmHg, pulse 62/min, respirations 14/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. On
examination, there is tenderness over the humerus and elbow with weakness in wrist extension, but the
left upper extremity has a full, painless range of motion. Radiographs reveal a mid-shaft humeral
fracture and a small, non-displaced olecranon fracture. The patient is admitted to the medical floor. On
hospital day 14, he reports a "pins and needles" sensation in his hand, numbness over the ring and
little fingers of the left hand, and mild atrophy of the interossei muscles. What is the most likely cause of
his current symptoms? Answer Choices: (A) Delayed-onset compartment syndrome (B) Cubital tunnel
compression from post-traumatic edema (C) Compression at Guyon canal (D) Nerve root compression
(E) Post-traumatic neuroma formation (F) Compression at the carpal tunnel (G) Traumatic humerus
injury (H) Thoracic outlet syndrome from trauma (I) Traumatic elbow injury (J) Delayed ulnar nerve
subluxation
 A. Traumatic elbow injury
B. Nerve root compression
C. Cubital tunnel compression from post-traumatic edema
D. Delayed ulnar nerve subluxation
E. Thoracic outlet syndrome from trauma
F. Compression at Guyon canal
G. Post-traumatic neuroma formation
H. Compression at the carpal tunnel
I. Delayed-onset compartment syndrome
J. Traumatic humerus injury
